name: Stellite-Crown
description: Stellite-Crown dominates its system like a monarch holding court, a banded sphere of silver and pale violet wrapped in a ring system that spans nearly a million kilometers. The rings are composed of ice crystals laced with metallic dust, refracting starlight into prismatic halos that shift and shimmer as the planet rotates. Beneath the cloud tops, perpetual storm systems churn in counterrotating bands, their cyclonic eyes large enough to swallow terrestrial worlds whole.

From the observation deck of any vessel in orbit, the view is simultaneously beautiful and oppressive. The planet's immense gravity well tugs at the inner ear, a subliminal reminder that the serene cloudscape below conceals crushing pressures and winds that exceed the speed of sound. The rings sing in radio frequencies, a faint hiss of particle collisions that crews on long helium-3 extraction runs describe as hypnotic, a white noise that blurs the boundary between wakefulness and dream.

The derelict station in high orbit was a helium-3 processing facility operated by the Kessler-Yun Combine until a magnetic pole reversal sent a radiation pulse through the facility and killed the fusion containment. The crew evacuated, but the station's automated systems partially rebooted years later, and it now drifts in a slowly decaying orbit, its running lights blinking in patterns that do not match any standard protocol. Salvage teams have boarded twice; both reported finding the interior rearranged in ways that do not match the original schematics.

The helium-3 reserves in Stellite-Crown's upper atmosphere are among the richest surveyed in the sector, enough to fuel a fleet for centuries. Several corporations maintain skimmer operations in the cloud tops, their harvest drones dipping into the atmosphere on tethered runs before winching back to orbital platforms. The magnetic anomalies make navigation treacherous, and the derelict station's decaying orbit will eventually bring it into the ring system, scattering debris across the primary extraction lanes in an event that could shut down harvesting operations for years.
